cards.back: $g(\mathbf{x})=\sum_i x_i$; $y=1$ if $g\ge\theta$, else 0. Any **inhibitory** input on → $y=0$. Threshold $\theta$ is hand-coded.

cards.front: AND / OR thresholds in an MP neuron
cards.back: AND of $n$ inputs → $\theta=n$ (all must fire). OR → $\theta=1$ (any one). NOR → inhibitory inputs, $\theta=0$.
Perceptron adds **learnable weights**, a **learnable bias** ($w_0=-\theta$), and **real-valued inputs**. Both give linear, binary decisions.
If $x\in P$ but $w\cdot x<0$: $w\leftarrow w+x$. If $x\in N$ but $w\cdot x\ge0$: $w\leftarrow w-x$. Converges **iff data is linearly separable**.

cards.front: Why does a single perceptron fail on XOR?
cards.back: XOR is **not linearly separable** — its four truth-table inequalities contradict. A 2-layer network of perceptrons can represent any Boolean function.
Input (no computation, #units = #features) → Hidden (core of learning, finds complex patterns) → Output (final result). >1 hidden layer = Deep NN; fully-connected = MLP.
Step output is hard & **non-differentiable** (blocks gradient descent). Sigmoid $\sigma(z)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-z}}$ is smooth, differentiable, in $(0,1)$ → a **probability**.
**MSE** $=\frac1m\sum(y-\hat y)^2$ for regression. **Cross-entropy** $=-\sum y\log\hat y$ for classification (probability outputs).
Pre-activation $a=\mathbf{w}^T\mathbf{x}+b$; activation $h=\sigma(a)$. Weight matrix shape = (#prev-layer neurons) × (#current-layer neurons). Weights init **randomly**.
$x_{new}=x-\eta\nabla v$. $\eta$ too small → slow; too large → overshoot/diverge; at a local min, gradient 0 → stuck.
Output: $\delta_j=(t_j-o_j)\,o_j(1-o_j)$. Hidden: $\delta_j=o_j(1-o_j)\sum_{k\in Downstream}\delta_k w_{kj}$. Update: $\Delta w_{ji}=\eta\,\delta_j x_{ji}$.
Sigmoid derivative $\le0.25$; multiplied across layers → gradients → 0, so early layers barely learn. **Fix: ReLU.**

cards.front: Three ways to avoid overfitting in NNs
cards.back: (1) **Validation set** — keep weights with least val error. (2) **Dropout** — randomly drop neurons. (3) **Early stopping** — halt before val error rises.
Stacking only linear layers collapses to one linear map (just linear regression). Non-linearity lets the network learn complex patterns.
ReLU $=\max(0,x)$, range $[0,\infty)$, but **dying ReLU**. Leaky ReLU $=\max(ax,x)$, $a\approx0.01$ fixes it. Softmax $=\frac{e^{z_i}}{\sum e^{z_j}}$, multi-class output, sums to 1.
Binary output → sigmoid; multi-class output → softmax; hidden layers → ReLU (or tanh); dead neurons → Leaky ReLU. Never sigmoid deep in a net.

cards.front: Batch vs SGD vs Mini-batch GD
cards.back: Batch: update after all data (stable, slow, memory-heavy). SGD: per example (noisy, escapes local minima). Mini-batch: per batch (32/64/128…) — the standard.
EWA: $V_t=\beta V_{t-1}+(1-\beta)O_t$. Momentum: EWA of **gradients** (damps oscillation). RMSProp: EWA of **squared gradients**, step $=\frac{dW}{\sqrt{S_{dW}}+\epsilon}$.
Adam = Momentum (1st moment $V$) + RMSProp (2nd moment $S$) + **bias correction** $\frac{V}{1-\beta_1^t}$. Defaults: $\alpha=0.001,\ \beta_1=0.9,\ \beta_2=0.999,\ \epsilon=10^{-8}$.
Decision $W^Tx+b=0$; support planes $=\pm1$. Constraint $y_i(W^Tx_i+b)\ge1$. Margin width $=\frac{2}{\|W\|}$.
$\min_{W,b}\tfrac12\|W\|^2$ s.t. $y_i(W^Tx_i+b)\ge1$. Convex quadratic program; maximising margin ⟺ minimising $\tfrac12\|W\|^2$.
Primal feasibility $g(X)\ge0$; dual feasibility $\lambda\ge0$; **complementary slackness** $\lambda g(X)=0$; stationarity $\nabla L=0$.

cards.front: SVM dual: W and support vectors
cards.back: $W=\sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i$. Points off the gutter have $\alpha_i=0$; **support vectors** are the $\alpha_i\ne0$ points on the margin — they alone define $W$.
Training points appear only inside **dot products** → enables the **kernel trick**, and it's more efficient (e.g. SMO).
Linear $x\cdot x'$; Polynomial $(x\cdot x'+c)^d$; RBF/Gaussian $e^{-\gamma\|x-x'\|^2}$. Try **RBF first**. High degree / high $\gamma$ → overfitting risk.
Slack $\xi_i$: 0 = outside margin; 0–1 = inside but correct; >1 = misclassified. $\min\tfrac12\|W\|^2+C\sum\xi_i$. Large C → narrow margin (hard, overfit); small C → wide (soft).
Parallel weak learners on **bootstrap** samples (sample with replacement), combined by vote/average. Each sample ≈ 63% of data ($(1-1/n)^n\to1/e$). Reduces variance ($\sigma^2/n$).
The ~37% not in a bootstrap sample. Score each point with the trees that didn't see it → free validation estimate, no separate val set.
Bagging: parallel, equal weights, reduces variance (Random Forest). Boosting: sequential, reweight misclassified ↑, reduces bias (AdaBoost, Gradient Boost).
Start with mean of $y$; compute residuals $y-\hat y$; fit a weak learner to the **residuals**; update $\hat y \leftarrow \hat y + \eta\cdot$learner; repeat. (AdaBoost reweights points instead.)
Bootstrap sample + **random R<M features** per tree → diverse trees; majority vote. OOB error for validation. No pruning, robust to outliers, overfitting not a problem.
